commit.message:
docs(wasm): npm trusted publishing works; by-hand is the fallback (#4975)

The @vowpalwabbit scope registration exists now, and wasm_v0.0.10 proved the
automatic path works: that run authenticated and was rejected only because
0.0.10 had been published by hand twenty minutes earlier. A publish with no
credential fails ENEEDAUTH before the registry is asked about the version, so
reaching a duplicate-version error is evidence authentication succeeded.

The docs still said "Blocked as of 9.11.7" and presented publishing by hand
as the path, which had it backwards, and invites the reasonable but wrong
conclusion that npm releases need someone holding a token.

They do not. publish_npm requests id-token: write, GitHub mints a short-lived
OIDC token for that one run, npm exchanges it for publish rights. wasm.yml
references no secrets at all, and the repository holds no npm token:

  publish_npm permissions: {contents: read, id-token: write}
  secrets.* anywhere in wasm.yml: False
  repo secrets matching npm/node: none

So npm now holds fewer credentials than Maven Central, which needs a Portal
token and a GPG key. Releasing npm is a tag push.

The by-hand procedure stays, retitled as the fallback it is: for a lapsed
registration, or publishing from a machine where there is no OIDC to
exchange. It notes what it costs -- a granular token with 2FA bypass -- and
that CI would have published the byte-identical artifact from a tag push with
no credential at all.

The release checklist loses its last "still needs hands" section. What is
left that needs a person: write the changelog, and decide to ship.
